:::{#exm-fubini-fail-tonelli}

#### When neither Tonelli's nor Fubini's condition is satisfied

The same function $f(x, y) = (x^2 - y^2)/(x^2 + y^2)^2$ from
@exm-fubini-fail illustrates a case where neither the hypothesis of
@thm-tonelli-measure nor that of @thm-fubini-measure is satisfied.

**Why the hypotheses fail:**
$\iint_R |f|\,dA = \infty$, which violates the absolute-integrability
hypothesis of @thm-fubini-measure.
Switching to polar coordinates $(r, \angpar)$ near the origin, the
integrand satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
|f(x, y)| &= \abs{x^2 - y^2}/(x^2 + y^2)^2 \\
&= \abs{\cos 2\angpar}/r^2,
\end{aligned}
$$

so

$$
\ba
\iint_R |f|\,dA
&\ge \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^{\smallconst}
   \frac{\abs{\cos 2\angpar}}{r^2}\, r\,dr\,d\angpar\\
&= \paren{\int_0^{\pi/2}\abs{\cos 2\angpar}\,d\angpar}
       \int_0^{\smallconst} \frac{dr}{r}\\
&= +\infty,
\ea
$$

since $\int_0^{\smallconst} dr/r$ diverges.
Therefore $\iint_R |f|\,dA = \infty$,
and the hypothesis of @thm-fubini-measure is not satisfied.
(The hypothesis of @thm-tonelli-measure also fails: $f$ takes both positive
and negative values, so it is not nonnegative a.e.)
The unequal iterated integrals from @exm-fubini-fail are thus consistent
with both theorems: neither one applies.

[@wp:fubini]

:::
